paper_claims.claim: In Fama-MacBeth regressions, the coefficient on intermediate-horizon past performance (r_12,7) is roughly twice that on recent past performance (r_6,2), and the difference is statistically significant.
MOM_12,7 is more profitable than MOM_6,2 (1.20% vs 0.67% per month) and retains a significant FF4 alpha (0.54, t=3.78) while MOM_6,2's four-factor alpha is insignificant (-0.05, t=-0.37).

In 5x5 independent double sorts, return spreads along the intermediate-horizon dimension are roughly twice those along the recent dimension, and conditional 12-7 strategies within r_6,2 quintiles dominate the reverse construction.

The disparity between intermediate-horizon and recent momentum is especially acute among large stocks: within the largest NYSE size quintile MOM_12,7 earns about 10% per year while MOM_6,2 is insignificant.

Momentum in other asset classes is likewise driven by intermediate-horizon past performance: FF-49 industry tertile strategies show 12-7 significant (0.57) vs 6-2 insignificant relative to UMD and to the 12-7 strategy.
Earnings momentum does not explain the result: adding SUE to the FM regressions leaves r_12,7 significant (0.99/0.94) while r_6,2 becomes even more insignificant (0.28/0.16).

tables.description: Fama-MacBeth regressions of returns on r_12,7 and r_6,2 with r_1,0, log(ME), log(BM) controls (slope x10^2 and t-stats)
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct FM cross-sectional regression machinery: monthly cross-sections, winsorized 1%/99% independent variables, tiered book-equity construction, June-aligned BM lagged 6 months, and the r_12,7-r_6,2 reparameterization test (whose coefficient must equal b(r12,7)-b(r62) of the same regression). Committed columns Late/Third/Fourth cover the Compustat era; the Whole/Early/First/Second columns need DFF (2000) book equity for 1927-1949, unavailable in the catalog.
tables.paper_quote: This table reports results from Fama-MacBeth regressions of firms’ returns on past performance, measured at horizons 12 to seven months ( $r_{12,7}$ ) and six to two months ( $r_{6,2}$ ). Regressions include controls for prior month’s performance ( $r_{1,0}$ ), size (log(ME)), and book-to-market (log(BM)). (L167-169)

tables.description: Time-series regressions of MOM_12,7 (specs 1-4) and MOM_6,2 (specs 5-8) on MKT, FF3, and FF4 factors, 1927-2010
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates correct VW decile (NYSE breaks) winner-minus-loser strategy construction from the CRSP universe and correct factor regression setup against the Fama-French factors plus UMD. The FF4 alpha contrast (0.54 significant vs -0.05 insignificant) is the paper's headline strategy-level claim.
tables.paper_quote: This table presents results of time-series regressions employing the returns to momentum strategies constructed using intermediate horizon and recent past performance. $MOM_{n,m}$ is the returns of the winner-minus-loser strategy (deciles, employing NYSE breaks), where winners and losers are based on cumulative returns from $n$ to $m$ months (inclusive) prior to portfolio formation. The sample period covers January 1927 through December 2010. (L303-305)

tables.description: Conditional momentum strategies 1969-2010: MOM_12,7 within each r_6,2 quintile and MOM_6,2 within each r_12,7 quintile - mean returns and FF3+MOM_12,7 alphas
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates the conditional (within-quintile) construction: quintile W-L sorts on one signal constructed within each quintile of the other. Distinct from T4's independent sort; validates the claim that intermediate-horizon momentum survives neutralization on recent performance while the converse fails.
tables.paper_quote: This table shows the average returns to the five winner-minus-loser portfolios in each direction from the double sort on recent and intermediate horizon past performances ( $r_{6,2}$ and $r_{12,7}$ ), and results from time series regressions employing these strategies’ returns. The sample covers January 1969 to December 2010. (L1485-1487)

tables.description: Industry momentum spanning tests: FF-49-industry tertile (top/bottom 30%) EW strategies on r_12,7 and r_6,2 regressed on UMD and each other, 1927-2010
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates construction of VW FF-49 industry portfolios from CRSP SIC codes and the tertile EW momentum sort over non-stock assets - the first test that the intermediate-vs-recent term structure extends beyond individual equities.
tables.paper_quote: $MOM_{n,m}^{indus}$ is the returns to the winner-minus-loser portfolio (tertiles), where winners and losers are based on cumulative returns from $n$ to $m$ months (inclusive) prior to portfolio formation. The sample period covers January 1927 through December 2010. (L1953-1955)

tables.description: FM regressions of returns on r_12,2 / r_12,7 / r_6,2 and SUE with r_1,0, ln(ME), ln(BM) controls, 1973-2010 (8 specifications)
tables.replication_meaning: Demonstrates the quarterly-earnings extension: SUE from Compustat fundq (last quarterly earnings minus its 4-quarter average, scaled by assets), merged to CRSP monthly returns. Tests that earnings momentum absorbs recent-past-performance power but not intermediate-horizon power.
tables.paper_quote: This table reports results of Fama-MacBeth regressions of firms’ returns on past performance variables ( $r_{12,2}$ , $r_{12,7}$ , and $r_{6,2}$ ) and standardized unexpected earnings (SUE, defined here as the deviation of a firm’s most recent quarterly earnings from its average earnings over the previous four quarters, scaled by assets). [...] The sample period covers January 1973 through December 2010 (L2585-2587)
